title: The Mathematics Under Cryptography
description: Walk the Hall of Foundations in teaching order — the number theory, hardness assumptions, and structures every modern key stands on, from clock arithmetic to lattices and pairings.

stops.label: Modular Arithmetic
stops.note: Start with the clock: Z/nZ, primitive roots, and the cyclic group Diffie–Hellman lives inside (§143).

stops.label: Group Theory
stops.note: Generators, order, cyclic structure — the grammar of nearly every public-key scheme (§149).

stops.label: Finite Fields
stops.note: Arithmetic mod a prime, where the elliptic curve shatters into a scatter and the discrete log gets hard (§142).

stops.label: The Prime Number Theorem
stops.note: Why RSA can find a 2048-bit prime in moments — the one theorem that is genuinely load-bearing (§144).

stops.label: Euler & Fermat
stops.note: The theorem that makes RSA decryption undo encryption. Watch a message round-trip (§145).

stops.label: Elliptic Curves over R
stops.note: The group law drawn by hand — a gentle first look before the curve moves to a finite field (§150).

stops.label: The Ground Beneath the Curve
stops.note: The modularity theorem and the deep number theory ECC inherits (§141).

stops.label: The One-Way Function
stops.note: Multiply in a blink; factor and sweat. The conceptual keystone everything is downstream of (§146).

stops.label: Reduction & Proof
stops.note: What "provably as hard as factoring" actually claims — and what it quietly assumes (§148).

stops.label: Information & Entropy
stops.note: Shannon's measure of surprise: why the one-time pad is perfect and key length is destiny (§151).

stops.label: The Random Oracle
stops.note: Flip one input bit, scramble half the output — the hash assumption every signature stands on (§154).

stops.label: Lattices & the SVP
stops.note: Drag a basis, hunt the shortest vector — the ground the post-quantum standards stand on (§147).

stops.label: The Closest Vector Problem
stops.note: Round to the nearest lattice corner — right with the secret basis, wrong with the public one. This is ML-KEM decryption (§152).

stops.label: Polynomial Rings
stops.note: R_q = Z_q[X]/(X^n+1): the structured lattice inside ML-KEM and ML-DSA (§153).

stops.label: Polynomial Interpolation
stops.note: k points fix a curve — the heart of Shamir's Secret Sharing and threshold signatures (§155).

stops.label: Bilinear Pairings
stops.note: e(aP,bQ) = e(P,Q)^ab — verify hidden scalars without revealing them; the magic under zk-SNARKs (§156).
